parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime shows no trans-specific criminal offence: the 2019 same-sex law was repealed in 2020, the 2024 constitution rejected re-criminalisation and added privacy, and the record documents no state-sponsored harassment of LGBTQ+ people. Against that, the dossier documents occasional police use of 'breaches of modesty' charges against gender-nonconforming presentations, common individual harassment with no gender-identity anti-discrimination law and no LGR, and LGBTI groups unable to register — societal hostility with thin recourse (tier 3), under a military regime whose recent criminalisation episode shows volatility. Border screening, document-marker handling, facilities and care are not_documented: open questions, not exposures. No universal-exposure measure or trans-specific violence record exists here. Severity if outed is arrest/harassment level, not imprisonment-or-death.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. The inventory contains no information on airport or border screening, document gender markers, or differential treatment of gender-nonconforming travellers at ports of entry.
entry_documents.protection: No documented trans-specific entry restriction; same-sex conduct has been lawful since the 2020 repeal and the constitution adds privacy protection (Article 18).
entry_documents.interaction: An open question: an entry mismatch could theoretically flow into modesty-charge policing, but no such pathway is sourced.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Police are reported to make occasional 'breaches of modesty' charges against gender-nonconforming presentations and same-sex couples; the same source calls this misuse not widespread. Historical arrests under the repealed 2019 law involved bribe-for-release.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: The source states state-sponsored harassment of LGBTQ+ people as a group is not present; no prosecution for gender expression is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Under the post-2023 military regime, neutral morality charges could escalate during an identity check, but no documented custody-placement or strip-search rules exist.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No facility, bathroom, custody-placement or ward-placement rule for gender-nonconforming people appears anywhere in the record.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Open question only: absence of sourcing is not evidence that facilities are safe or unsafe.

care_services.exposure: Not documented for visitors. Conversion therapies (religious and ritualistic) are described as widespread, but aimed at residents; no visitor care-denial is sourced.
care_services.protection: Sexual orientation and sexual life are sensitive personal data under Law No. 025/2023 — a narrow data-protection ground, not a service protection.
care_services.interaction: An emergency admission could expose identity, but ward or treatment-refusal practice for trans visitors is unsourced.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Occasional police misuse of neutral 'modesty' charges against gender-nonconforming presentation; public opinion on decriminalisation was sharply divided and civil society pressed unsuccessfully for re-criminalisation in 2024.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Constitutional privacy (Article 18) and the 2024 referendum's rejection of re-criminalisation; source states state-sponsored harassment is not present.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Military governance since the 2023 coup means police discretion operates under an unelected regime, but no trans-targeted directive is documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. Nothing in the record addresses a transgender parent or a minor travelling with one.
minors_guardians.interaction: The entrenched opposite-sex marriage definition (Article 16) denies recognition to locally-read same-sex couples, which could affect a travelling family's legal standing, but its application to a trans visitor's family is unsourced.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Harassment by individuals is described as common and LGBTQIA+ stigmatisation is documented; involuntary conversion therapies are widespread (single encyclopedic source, uncorroborated).
street_violence_police_response.protection: No state-sponsored group harassment documented; no trans-specific killings or violence statistics appear in the inventory at all.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: No anti-discrimination law means a visitor harassed in public has no identity-based remedy, though ordinary assault law presumably applies — unverified.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No gender-identity discrimination protection, no legal gender recognition, LGBTI groups cannot register — recourse machinery for trans people is absent or blocked.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Constitutional privacy protections (Article 18) and sensitive-data treatment of sexual orientation; the 2019 offence was reversed through normal legislative process.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Thin formal recourse plus a military regime weakens whatever paper protection exists; recurring 'modesty' misuse is unremedied in the record.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.55-C documents a universal exposure (ward placement by document sex) with partial remedies. This dossier documents no universal exposure at all — no facility, custody or border rule — but also no remedy machinery. Lacking a tier-1 universal exposure pushes this case slightly above 0.55-C, while thin recourse and common harassment keep it from 0.65.

0.65-A has a documented mistreatment episode but national equality law, an intervention and a working complaint producing apology and compensation. This dossier has comparable mid-level exposure (occasional modesty charges, harassment) but no equality law, no identity-based complaint route and no documented relief — so it sits below 0.65-A.

0.45-D's police registration and nightly hotel databases are universal exposures reaching every visitor. This dossier documents no registration, surveillance or reporting regime; its exposures are occasional police charge misuse and individual harassment. It is materially safer than 0.45-D.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller here faces a documented pattern of mid-level, non-state-group exposure: occasional police use of neutral morality charges against gender-nonconforming presentation, common individual harassment, and no identity-based legal recourse — under a military regime that recently decriminalised same-sex conduct amid sharp public division. There is no trans-specific criminal offence, no documented state-sponsored harassment, no universal-exposure measure (border, documents, facilities, custody, care all not_documented), and no trans-violence record. Severity if outed is arrest-and-harassment tier, not imprisonment-or-execution. Positives are documented but paper-thin (constitutional privacy, 2020 repeal); negatives are documented but described as not widespread. This combination — hostility with thin recourse, absence of criminalisation, unknowns left as questions — lands in the upper Elevated / lower Reduced range at 0.57.
